name: rhodium
notes: OTC quote (Johnson Matthey / LBMA).  Reference $320k/kg = $9,950/oz (May 8 2026 spot).  Trace PGM in M-type / iron-meteorite analogues.

name: iridium
notes: OTC quote.  Reference $257,206/kg = $8,000/oz, the Q1-2026 all-time high in the Johnson Matthey PGM Market Report (May 2026), the latest JM base price published before this row's date.  Trace PGM in iron-meteorite analogues.

name: gold
notes: COMEX gold front-month.  Reference $150k/kg = ~$4,700/oz; gold ran from $3,335 (May 2025) to $4,732 (May 2026) per Reuters analyst consensus.

name: ruthenium
notes: OTC quote.  Reference $56,264/kg = $1,750/oz, the Q1-2026 all-time high in the Johnson Matthey PGM Market Report (May 2026), as for iridium; JM's end-2025 record was $1,275/oz.  Trace PGM.

name: platinum
notes: NYMEX platinum front-month.  Reference $61,472/kg = $1,912/oz, the LBMA platinum price on 2026-05-29.

name: palladium
notes: NYMEX palladium front-month.  Reference $48k/kg = $1,495/oz spot (May 2026, LBMA via lppm.com).

name: osmium
notes: Specialty quote; very illiquid.

name: germanium
notes: Zone-refined germanium, 2024 ~$2,000-3,000/kg (USGS MCS 2025).  Siderophile: iron meteorites carry 0.1-500 ppm.

name: silver
notes: COMEX silver front-month.  Reference $2,436.5/kg = $75.78/oz, the LBMA silver price on 2026-05-29.

name: rhenium
notes: Rhenium metal pellets, 2024 ~$1,200-1,600/kg (USGS MCS 2025).  Highly siderophile, tracks osmium in meteoritic metal.

name: gallium
notes: High-purity refined gallium, $500/kg in 2024 and $450-625/kg over 2020-2024 (USGS MCS 2025, average unit value of imports).  Iron meteorites carry 2-100 ppm.

name: tungsten
notes: APT at the start of 2025: Rotterdam $331/mtu (USGS MCS 2026, which says it rose to $675 during 2025, ~$85/kg W) = ~$42/kg of contained W (1 mtu = 7.93 kg W, MCS 2025).  MCS 2025 withholds the 2024 price.  The cell is the start-of-2025 level, matching the row date.

name: molybdenum
notes: Molybdic oxide ~$20/lb of contained Mo in 2024 (USGS MCS 2025) = ~$44/kg.

name: cobalt
notes: LME cobalt cash; trace constituent of FeNi alloys.

name: nickel
notes: LME nickel.  Reference $18,806/t, the World Bank Pink Sheet monthly average for May 2026.

name: copper
notes: COMEX copper front-month.  Reference $13,543/t, the World Bank Pink Sheet monthly average for May 2026.

name: titanium
notes: Titanium sponge, $13/kg in 2024 and $10.6-12.4/kg in 2020-2023 (USGS MCS 2025, landed duty-paid import value).  Structural.

name: chromium
notes: Aluminothermic chromium metal, ~$10-12/kg (USGS MCS 2025 carries ferrochrome and metal).  Stainless alloying.

name: phosphorus
notes: Elemental (P4) trade price, ~$3,000/t; USGS lists phosphate rock, not the element.  In space: fertiliser for agriculture.

name: ammonia
notes: Anhydrous ammonia, US Gulf FOB $440 per SHORT ton in 2024 (USGS MCS 2025 nitrogen) = $485 per metric ton.  Solid density.  In space: nitrogen for atmospheres, fertiliser, and resistojet propellant.

name: iron
notes: Priced as refined steel scrap: No. 1 heavy melting composite, delivered, $319/t average for 2025 (USGS MCS 2026), within its $303-366/t monthly range for Jan-Nov 2025.  Asteroid mining produces refined iron from nickel-iron alloy, NOT iron ore — so the relevant sale price is steel scrap / refined metal, not the $0.10/kg iron-ore benchmark.

name: sulfur
notes: USGS MCS 2025 elemental sulfur, ~$80-100/t in 2024.  In space: sulfur concrete binder and sulfuric-acid leachant.

name: carbon dioxide
notes: Industrial liquid CO2, ~$50-150/t; not a USGS commodity.  Solid density.  In space: the carbon feed for Sabatier methane and a life-support buffer gas.

name: water
notes: Price depends entirely on where the water is SOLD, not on the asteroid — see DELIVERY_DESTINATIONS. Set MINERAL_CONFIG.delivery_destination to 'leo' or 'cislunar' to price it as launch cost avoided; the default 'earth_surface' prices it as what it is once landed, which is bulk industrial water.

name: spinel
notes: Mg-Al oxide; high-T refractory.

name: organics
notes: Complex organic macromolecules (kerogen-like).

name: carbon
notes: Amorphous / graphitic carbon (not gem diamond).

name: merrillite
notes: The anhydrous Ca phosphate of ordinary chondrites, ~0.4 wt%.  Priced as it is as phosphate rock (USGS MCS 2025, ~$100/t in 2024) and taken apart for its P.

name: chlorapatite
notes: The Cl-apatite of ordinary chondrites, ~0.2 wt%.  Priced as phosphate rock, as merrillite is.

name: plagioclase
notes: Feldspar group; basaltic-crust marker.

name: oxides
notes: Generic metal-oxide bulk.

name: hibonite
notes: A refractory CAI oxide in CV/CO chondrites.  Its aluminium is a light metal whose extraction is deferred, so it is priced as rock, as spinel is.

name: olivine
notes: Mg-Fe silicate.  Fa10 mean; bulk industrial use only.

name: pyroxene
notes: Mg-Fe-Ca chain silicate.

name: orthopyroxene
notes: Mg-Fe end of the pyroxene series.

name: enstatite
notes: Mg-pyroxene end-member; E-chondrite analogue.

name: phyllosilicates
notes: Hydrated clays, priced as dehydrated rock: their bound water is the catalog's ice fraction.

name: silicates
notes: Catch-all rock-forming silicate bulk.

name: carbonates
notes: Calcite, dolomite, breunnerite: 2-5 wt% of CI chondrites.  Calcining releases the CO2.

name: nickel-iron
notes: Iron-meteorite analogue (IIIAB octahedrite mean) — Fe + Ni + trace PGMs + Au.  Total PGM ≈ 37 ppm matches siderite literature.  Yields cover all 6 PGMs as of v1.1.2.

name: magnetite
notes: Iron-oxide ore; priced as Fe content.

name: troilite
notes: Iron sulfide, standing for all Fe sulfides (troilite, pyrrhotite).  Yields Fe and S.

name: schreibersite
notes: Fe-Ni phosphide, 1.5-3% of iron-meteorite and enstatite-chondrite metal.  The phosphorus source in an asteroid.

name: chromite
notes: Cr-Fe spinel oxide; ~0.5 wt% of ordinary chondrites, ~1% of HEDs.

name: ilmenite
notes: Fe-Ti oxide; ~1 wt% of eucrites.  The same mineral lunar ISRU plans reduce for oxygen.

name: kamacite
notes: Low-Ni body-centred Fe-Ni (~6.5 wt% Ni): most of an iron meteorite's metal and an H chondrite's.  Derived from the IIIAB nickel-iron row; Co-richer, Pt/Pd/Au/Cu-poorer.

name: taenite
notes: High-Ni face-centred Fe-Ni (~30 wt% Ni, with plessite): most of an LL chondrite's metal.  Derived from the IIIAB row; carries the taenite-loving Pt, Pd, Au and Cu.

name: tetrataenite
notes: Ordered FeNi (~50 wt% Ni) in slowly cooled chondrite metal. A rare-earth-free magnet candidate with no market to price, so priced by its yields at taenite's trace contents.

name: cohenite
notes: Iron carbide with ~3 wt% Ni, in iron meteorites (IAB, IIAB) and some chondrite metal.  Steel-like; yields Fe and Ni.

name: pyrrhotite
notes: The Fe(1-x)S sulfide of CI, CM and Tagish Lake, where troilite is the ordinary chondrites'.  Yields Fe and S.

name: pentlandite
notes: The nickel sulfide: where a CI or CK chondrite's nickel is, rather than in metal.  The terrestrial Ni ore mineral.

name: niningerite
notes: Mg-rich monosulfide of the EH enstatite chondrites, ~2 wt%. Its Mg and Mn are not priced.

name: oldhamite
notes: Calcium sulfide of enstatite chondrites and aubrites, formed only in very reducing conditions.  Its Ca is not priced.

name: daubreelite
notes: Fe-Cr sulfide of enstatite chondrites and aubrites, and lamellae in iron-meteorite troilite: chromium as a sulfide.

name: perovskite
notes: A CAI oxide in CV/CO chondrites (K, L types).  Titanium as ilmenite gives it; its Ca is not priced.

name: sperrylite
notes: Pt arsenide (Pt 56.6 wt%) — dominant terrestrial Pt ore.  Documented in some iron meteorites and in Sudbury impact-melt-class material.  Arsenic is toxic but recoverable; ignored in valuation.

name: laurite
notes: Ru sulfide (Ru 61.2 wt%) with trace Ir / Os substitution.  Found in PGM-bearing chromites and rare iron-meteorite phases.

name: awaruite
notes: Ni-rich Fe-Ni alloy (Ni 75.9 wt%, Fe 24.1 wt%) with concentrated PGMs (5× nickel-iron baseline).  Terrestrial analog: Josephine / Mojave ophiolites.  Documented in some ureilites and rare meteoritic phases.  Use as a high-grade target where spectral data suggests PGM enrichment beyond bulk Fe-Ni.

name: native-pgm
notes: Mixed native PGM alloy (Pt 70 wt%, Pd 15, Ir 8, Os 5, Ru 1, Rh 1).  Implied value ≈ $55k/kg — by far the richest mineral phase in the catalog.  Extremely rare; documented as nuggets in some ureilites, rare iron meteorites, and Os-Ir-Ru alloys.  Reserved for high-confidence per-asteroid override use cases.
